explanation: For a power series solution of f^{(n)} = g(z, f, …, f^{(n−1)}) with g defined at the initial point, ω-integrality with ω(p)/p → ∞ implies bounded denominators. This is (3) ⇒ (2) of Lam–Litt (arXiv:2501.13175) Conjecture 1.1.1, and it follows from the conjectured (3) ⇒ (1) plus Eisenstein. IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE writes g = p/q with q nonvanishing at the initial values, matching footnote 1. The name says "algebraicity" but the conclusion is integrality; the docstring is accurate. The statement is faithful and open.
